title: Budget Billing (Levelized and Equal Payment Plans): Removal History and Re-Enrollment Across the Member's Accounts
content:
# Removal History and Re-Enrollment — Budget Billing (Levelized and Equal Payment Plans)

Credit and collections guidance for Budget Billing (Levelized and Equal Payment Plans).

## The rule

Removal history is read across the member's portfolio. No account of a member may enroll while the member has a removal in the window, so a removal on one account blocks every account of the member for the removal re-enrollment wait; a voluntary exit blocks only the account that exited, for the exit re-enrollment wait.

**A removal in the window** means a Budget Billing plan of the member, on any of the member's service accounts, that was removed from the plan for missed installments with a removal date that falls within the removal re-enrollment wait, counted as that many calendar months ending on the enrollment date. The wait is 12 months on every plan, so the window is the 12 calendar months ending on the enrollment date. The count of such plans must be zero for any account of the member to enroll.

**The exit re-enrollment wait** is 3 months on Levelized Billing Rolling Average and 12 months on every other plan.

## Basis of the judgement

- **Records, not statements.** Whether the member has a removal in the window is read from the cooperative's Budget Billing plan records for the member: the status each plan moved to and the date of its removal. What the member recalls about a past plan does not take the place of those records.
- **Whose records.** The member's records across every service account the member holds, not only the account now asking to enroll.
- **Point in time.** The window ends on the enrollment date and is read before the enrollment is made.

## Removal compared with voluntary exit

| Past event on a plan of the member | Accounts blocked | For how long |
|---|---|---|
| Removal from the plan for missed installments | Every account of the member | While the removal date is within the 12 calendar months ending on the enrollment date |
| Voluntary exit by the member | Only the account that exited | The exit re-enrollment wait: 3 months on Levelized Billing Rolling Average, 12 months on the other plans |

## Hypothetical cases

- *Hypothetical:* a member's shop meter was removed from Budget Billing Quarterly Review for missed installments, with a removal date four calendar months before the date on which the member's home meter would enroll. The removal date is within the 12 calendar months ending on the enrollment date, so the home meter may not enroll.
- *Hypothetical:* the same removal date falls on the enrollment date itself. The window ends on that date, so the removal is within it and the enrollment is blocked.
- *Hypothetical:* the removal date is 15 calendar months before the enrollment date. It is outside the 12-month window and is not counted.
- *Hypothetical:* a member left Budget Billing Annual Settle-Up voluntarily on a well meter. That exit blocks only the well meter; under this rule it places no block on the member's other accounts.
